Owned by the product pinecone-api-key detector since product main 2420e80 (redact-secret#766 and its ADR 2026-09-24-claim-a-legacy-pinecone-uuid-key-only-under-its-api-key-name): the UUID is redacted at high confidence under a Pinecone API-key name (PINECONE_API_KEY, pinecone_api_key, PINECONE_KEY, or api_key/apiKey/Api-Key on a line naming pinecone), and a bare UUID stays unclaimed. The detector reports it with the same pinecone_api_key finding type as pcsk_, so detectors stays empty: mapping the family to pinecone-api-key would merge it into that contract (#253). empiricalEvidence.uncertainty: Postman's docs state no PMAK- grammar (only the X-API-Key header and a postman-api-key variable). Its own Insights Agent redaction config fixes PMAK- + 24 lowercase hex + '-' + 34 lowercase hex, matching gitleaks and Nosey Parker, while trufflehog corroborates only the prefix and 59-byte width. The same Postman config also redacts a bare PMAK- + 24 hex value (L32). That pattern matches the id part of every full key, so the family reads it as a prefix-level scrub and keeps the 24-hex fragment as a non-credential near miss (settled by L72, a judgement). The benchmark claims only lowercase-hex keys. No issued key has been measured, and a second Postman credential (PMAT-) exists outside the contract (redact-secret#700).
supportedContexts: bare value (the PMAK- prefix is the only marker; no keyword required)
